plan.title: sec: four medium symlink/path-escape write sinks (scope planRef, issue cache, welcome audit, release markdown)

narratives.Description: This story implements the cited GitHub issue acceptance criteria in the scoped packages listed in swarm.file_scope. It includes regression tests and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased Fixed or Changed as appropriate.
narratives.Overview:
**Severity:** Medium (4 findings)
**Source:** Scheduled application-security review at `055bef735cf5`
**Related:** same symlink / path-escape trust-boundary class as #2413 / #2446 / #2447 / #2383; prior memory-write findings appear fixed and were not re-reported

## Summary

Four TypeScript engine write paths still allow repo- or input-controlled path escape when resolving lifecycle refs or writing well-known projections. A malicious repository author (or crafted `planRef` / `references[].uri`) can steer routine operator/agent commands into `mkdir` / `write` / `append` outside the intended tree.

`assertProjectionContained` (#2413) already guards newer projection surfaces; these four call sites were not covered.

---

### 1) Medium — Scope lifecycle `planRef` escapes the xbrief tree

**Location:** `packages/core/src/scope/vbrief-ref.ts`

**Attacker / input:** malicious `planRef` or `references[].uri` containing `..` segments or `file:///` absolute paths.

**Attack path:**
1. Victim runs `task scope:promote`, `scope:activate`, or `scope:complete`.
2. Lifecycle code resolves the ref via `resolveLifecycleArtifactRef` / `resolveVbriefRef`.
3. Escaping refs resolve outside the real lifecycle root; subsequent JSON rewrites write outside the xbrief tree.

**Impact:** scope lifecycle can rewrite JSON files outside the lifecycle tree under the victim account.

**Remediation:** contain `resolveLifecycleArtifactRef` / `resolveVbriefRef` under the real lifecycle root; reject absolute and escaping refs before any rewrite write.

---

### 2) Medium — Issue cache follows a repo-controlled `.deft-cache` symlink

**Location:** `packages/core/src/cache/operations.ts`

**Attacker / input:** a trackable `.deft-cache` → outside symlink (gitignore only matches `.deft-cache/`).

**Attack path:**
1. Victim clones the repo and runs cache put/fetch.
2. Cache operations `mkdir` + write issue cache files under the resolved cache root.
3. Without `lstat` / `realpath` containment, the symlink is followed outside the project.

**Impact:** issue cache files can be created outside the project tree under the victim account.

**Remediation:** apply `assertProjectionContained` (or equivalent Lstat/realpath) on the cache root before mkdir/write; refuse escaping symlinks.

---

### 3) Medium — Welcome audit follows `meta/policy-changes.log` symlink

**Location:** `packages/core/src/triage/welcome/writers.ts`

**Attacker / input:** a committed symlink at `meta/policy-changes.log` pointing to an outside file.

**Attack path:**
1. Victim runs `task triage:welcome --onboard`.
2. Welcome writers `appendFileSync` policy audit lines to the audit path.
3. The symlink is followed; lines land outside the project.

**Impact:** policy audit appends can overwrite or extend an attacker-chosen file outside the checkout.

**Remediation:** contain the audit path before append; use no-follow / atomic replace semantics.

---

### 4) Medium — Release/changelog writers follow root markdown symlinks

**Location:** `packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts`

**Attacker / input:** committed `CHANGELOG.md` / `ROADMAP.md` symlinks to writable paths outside the checkout.

**Attack path:**
1. Victim runs release or roadmap render.
2. Pipeline writes promoted changelog / rendered roadmap via `writeFileSync` (or equivalent) on the joined root paths.
3. Symlinks are followed; outside files are overwritten.

**Impact:** release/roadmap writes can overwrite attacker-chosen files outside the project tree with release content.

**Remediation:** apply projection containment before changelog/roadmap writes.

---

## Acceptance

- [ ] `resolveLifecycleArtifactRef` / `resolveVbriefRef` reject absolute and `..`-escaping refs; scope promote/activate/complete never rewrite JSON outside the real lifecycle root.
- [ ] Issue-cache put/fetch refuse when `.deft-cache` (or a parent) is a symlink or resolves outside the project root; no out-of-tree mkdir/write occurs.
- [ ] Welcome audit append refuses when `meta/policy-changes.log` is a symlink or resolves outside the project root; prefer no-follow / atomic replace.
- [ ] Release/changelog and roadmap writers refuse when `CHANGELOG.md` / `ROADMAP.md` are symlinks or resolve outside the project root; no out-of-tree overwrite occurs.
- [ ] Shared `assertProjectionContained` (or documented twin) covers `lstat` + parent walk + project-root / lifecycle-root prefix check before every affected write path.
- [ ] Regression tests cover: escaping `planRef` / `file:///` absolute refs; symlink-at-`.deft-cache`; symlink-at-`meta/policy-changes.log`; symlink-at-`CHANGELOG.md` / `ROADMAP.md` (and symlink-in-parent-path where applicable).

## Notes

Prefer one PR if `#2413` containment can be reused across all four sinks; otherwise tightly scoped PRs in the same conflict-safe cohort. Finding (1) is input-path escape (ref string), not only symlink-at-target — still the same containment class once resolved. Prior memory-write issues that appear fixed were intentionally not re-reported in this pass.

narratives.UserStory: As an operator running scope/cache/welcome/release verbs, I want path-escape sinks refused, so that crafted refs and symlinks cannot write outside the intended tree.

narrative.Acceptance: Given absolute or escaping planRef, when scope lifecycle resolves refs, then rewrites outside the lifecycle root are refused.
Given escaping .deft-cache or policy-changes.log symlinks, when cache/welcome writers run, then out-of-tree writes are refused.
Given CHANGELOG.md or ROADMAP.md symlinks escaping the project, when release writers run, then overwrites are refused.
